title: Questhand 101
subtitle: Start here: a short course on Questhand, made in Questhand

modules.title: A hello from your guide
modules.body: Press play for a short welcome (under 20 seconds). Then work through the cards in order.

modules.title: Watch: a 30-second tour
modules.body: The places you'll use most: the Map and Students (Settings is the third tab).

modules.title: Where are you starting from?
modules.body: There's no wrong answer: it only changes which cards you get next.

questions.text: How much have you used online course tools?
options: Never, this is new to me

modules.title: Start here: a course is a deck of cards
modules.body:
Each lesson is a short row of cards. A card is one small thing to do: read, watch, answer, make or discuss.

Students open one card at a time and see right away what comes next. You see every card at once on the Map.

modules.title: What your students see
modules.body:
Students get a board with today's lesson on top and the next card to play. Cards they've finished go on the Done pile; the rest wait in their hand.

Under the lesson's progress, small tags show only what needs them: cards to revise, overdue, due soon, to catch up, or an elective to choose. Starred cards are on My board. A card to read has Done, and Later to keep it for another time. My progress shows their scores and your feedback.

They never see a card that isn't meant for them. You'll try this yourself in Week 3 with Student View.

modules.title: Coming from another tool?
modules.body:
Two things are different here.

1. Everything is a card, so a lesson is quick to build and easy to rearrange: drag cards on the Map.
2. Answers can deal cards. The card a student gets next can depend on what they just answered, without any extra settings.

questions.text: Where do you see every card of the course at once, with the lines between them?
questions.explain: The Map shows each lesson as a row of cards, and the lines show which answer deals which card.

modules.title: Two kinds of card
modules.body:
Content cards hold something to read, watch or listen to.

Question cards ask something back. Under How students answer, pick Choices (a right answer, or a poll), Open answer, Worksheet, or Discussion.

modules.title: Watch: make your first card
modules.body: See a card made from start to finish, with a title, instructions and media.

modules.title: Card quiz
modules.body: Three quick questions. Your score decides what you get next.

questions.text: You want students to watch a video. Which card?
questions.explain: A Content card holds words, pictures, videos, links and recordings.

questions.text: Which card lets students vote, with no right answer?
questions.explain: A poll has no right answer; every vote counts.

questions.text: A student should write a paragraph or upload a photo. Which card?
questions.explain: An open answer card takes words, a drawing, a recording or a file.

modules.title: The card kinds again, side by side
modules.body:
- Content: something to read, watch or listen to.
- Choices with a right answer: checked at once (one answer, several, an order, or a short typed answer).
- Choices with no right answer: a poll.
- Open answer: students hand in words, a drawing, a recording or a file, and you give feedback.
- Worksheet: students fill in a copy of your text, each their own or one per group or class.
- Discussion: a shared wall where the class posts and replies.

modules.title: Ahead of the class: card groups
modules.body:
You got all three. The quiz you just took was a card group: several cards answered together, with one score.

To make one, press Group cards under the Map, tap the cards (or drag a box around them), then Make a card group. Next week you'll see how a score can deal cards.

modules.title: Your turn: plan a card
modules.body: Think of one lesson you'll teach soon. Which card would you start it with, and why? Write a few lines, or record yourself saying it.

modules.title: Five ways to ask
modules.body:
A Question card with Choices can ask in several ways. Set Has a right answer to Yes, then pick One answer, Several, Order or Short answer. Set it to No (a poll) for a vote.

Try each one below. Each student sees the choices in their own order, so the right one isn't always first.

questions.text: What can a Content card hold? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Grades come from Question cards; Content cards hold things to read, watch or listen to.

questions.text: Put the steps of making a branch in order.
options: Drag an answer's dot to a card
questions.explain: Question, answers, then drag each answer to the card it deals, and check it as a student.

questions.text: Which tab shows every card of the course at once, with its branches? (one word)
questions.explain: The Map: every lesson as a row of cards, and the lines between them.

modules.title: Math in a card
modules.body:
Write math between dollar signs and students see it typeset: $\frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}$, or $x^2 + y^2 = r^2$.

It works in a card's text, its question, its choices and the explanation. The editor shows how it will look under Students see.

modules.title: How is it going?
modules.body: Pick one, then press Submit vote. You can't change it after.

questions.text: How do you feel about building your first course?

modules.title: More help, just for you
modules.body: You said you need more help, so this card is yours. Start small: one lesson, three cards (something to read, one question, one branch). Then open Student View and try it as a student.

modules.title: Several questions, one card group
modules.body: Writing a quiz? On a Choices card, press + Add the next question. The next question goes on its own card, and the cards become a card group, answered together with one score.

weeks.title: Week 2 · Card trees and your course

modules.title: Why branch?
modules.body:
A class doesn't all need the same next step. Some need another example; some are ready for a challenge.

On the Map, each line runs from an answer to the card it deals. Students who pick that answer get the card; the others never see it.

modules.title: Watch: draw a branch
modules.body: Drag an answer's dot to make the card it deals. One answer can deal more than one card.

modules.title: Try a branch
modules.body: This card is a branch itself: each answer deals a different card.

questions.text: A student answers “I'm not sure yet”. What should they get next?
options: Another example, explained step by step
questions.explain: A short extra example, only for the students who need it, is what a branch is for.

modules.title: Yes: a short extra example
modules.body: That's the idea. Make the extra example a small card, and drag the “not sure” answer to it. Only those students get it.

modules.title: Why not the same card again?
modules.body: Showing the same card rarely helps. Give a different way in instead: another example, a video, a picture.

modules.title: Why not just move on?
modules.body: A student who isn't sure yet will likely be stuck on the next card too. A short detour card helps them catch up.

modules.title: Branch by score
modules.body:
A card group (or a quiz) can deal cards by score. Its score ranges show under it on the Map, such as below 60%, 60 to 99%, and 100%. Drag a range's dot to the card it deals, just like an answer.

Scores go by the student's best try, so a better retake deals the card for its new range.

modules.title: Deal a card in a later lesson
modules.body:
An answer can deal a card in another lesson: when you make the card, pick the lesson under New card in. Or click an answer's dot and choose Deal a card already made.

The student gets the card when they reach that lesson, with a note saying which answer opened it.

modules.title: Who gets a card
modules.body:
Open a card's panel and look under **Access**. It says who gets the card:

- **Everyone gets this card**: the usual.
- **Students get it from** an answer or a score range: set on the map, by drawing the line.
- **Only some students or groups…**: pick students by name, or whole groups. A group's card goes to whoever is in the group, also when the group changes (for example, after a sign-up poll).

Under it is the card's due date: **No due date** unless you pick one.

> In Week 3, one card in this course is only for the students who pick “Just exploring” in a sign-up poll.

modules.title: Sketch your own tree
modules.body: Draw (or describe) a small tree for one of your lessons: one question, its answers, and the card each answer deals. Use Draw if you like.

modules.title: Make a course
modules.body:
On your courses page, press New course. Give it a name (a subtitle is optional), then choose:

- Start blank: one empty week to fill yourself.
- Standard weeks: each week starts with a goal, an example, a quick check that deals a review or a stretch card, a task and a discussion. Change anything.

Press Create course, and you're on its Map.

modules.title: Weeks and lessons
modules.body:
Each lesson is a row on the Map, and lessons sit in weeks.

- The **+ Card** button on a lesson's row adds a card; **+ Lesson** at the end of the map adds a lesson.
- New week: from a template (give it a theme) or a Blank week.
- Click a lesson's name to rename it.
- A lesson's ⋯ menu: Duplicate lesson, Delete lesson, Add a lesson to the week, and Rename, Duplicate or Delete the week.

modules.title: Dates and today's lesson
modules.body:
Each lesson has a date chip: press Set date. The lesson for today says Today, and it's the one on top of every student's board.

To date them all at once, open a lesson's ⋯ menu → Schedule lessons from here…: pick the first class, the days class meets and any days off, and every lesson from there gets its date.

No dates? Use Make it today's lesson in the lesson's ⋯ menu when the class moves on.

A card can have its own due date too, under Access in its panel. **No due date** is where every card starts; pick Today, +3 days, +1 week, or any date. Students see it on the card, and a tag on their board says when something is due soon or overdue.

modules.title: Use a card again
modules.body:
Made a card you'll want again, like a weekly reflection or a check-in poll? In its panel, press Save to my cards (at the bottom). On a card group, that saves the group with its cards. To save a whole lesson, use its ⋯ menu → Save lesson to my cards.

Then, in any of your courses, add a card as usual (+ Card on a lesson, or an answer's dot) and choose Saved cards. Pick one to put down a copy, and change it as you like. The × beside one takes it off the list.

modules.title: Already have a plan written?
modules.body:
Settings → Back up and share → Import from a document… Upload your course plan, look over the weeks and cards Questhand proposes, untick what you don't want, and press Add.

The same place exports a course: Export course (.json) to keep a copy, or Export for Canvas / Moodle (.imscc).

questions.text: Your lessons have no dates. The class is moving on to lesson 3. What do you do?
options: Nothing: students move on by themselves
Lesson 3's ⋯ menu → Make it today's lesson
questions.explain: Today's lesson is the one on top of every student's board. Without dates, you choose it from the ⋯ menu.

modules.title: Watch: getting around the map
modules.body: The contents panel, picking cards with a box, moving cards, folding branches, and the trash.

modules.title: Move, pick and tidy
modules.body:
- Contents: point at the map's left edge (the bar with ›) to see every week and lesson. Click one to go there.
- Search: press / (or Search under the map) and type any word on a card; pick a result to go to it.
- Move a card: drag it along its row, or into another lesson.
- Pick several: drag a box on empty space (Shift adds more). Then make them a card group, or delete them.
- Pan: hold Space and drag.
- Zoom: − and + under the map, or pinch. The % button fits the map's width; press it again to see the whole course.
- Fold all / Unfold all hides or shows the cards answers deal.

modules.title: One undo for everything
modules.body:
Everything saves as you go (you'll see Saved at the top right).

- **Undo** (⌘Z or Ctrl+Z) and **Redo** (⇧⌘Z) sit at the top of the page, and the same buttons are at the top of a card's panel: one undo for every change, on the map or in a card.
- **History** (the clock beside them) lists your changes since you opened the course. Pick one to go back to before it.
- Delete a card: hold it until the cards jiggle and tap ⊖, or drag it onto the Trash. Cards only its answers deal go with it. The Trash keeps deleted cards to Restore.
- Delete a lesson or a week from its ⋯ menu. That one can't be undone, so you're asked first. Students' work stays saved.

modules.title: Keyboard shortcuts
modules.body:
Press ? on the course page for the full list. The ones you'll use most:

- 1 to 3: Map, Students, Settings.
- n: a new card in today's lesson.
- /: find a card.
- In a card's panel, [ and ] go to the previous and next card.
- On the map, the arrow keys move between cards, and Enter opens one.

questions.text: Put the steps of making a card group in order.
options: Tap the cards, or drag a box around them
Drag a score range to the card it deals
questions.explain: Group cards, pick the cards, make the group, then branch from its score ranges if you like.

modules.title: Format a card
modules.body:
## Text that's easy to read

A Text card can have **headings**, *emphasis*, lists, links, dividers and tables. Use the bar above the text box, or type the shortcuts: **⌘B** for bold, a line starting with - for a list.

> A callout like this one is good for a tip or the one idea students should keep.

| To make… | In the text box |
| --- | --- |
| A heading | H on the bar |
| A list | • or 1. on the bar |
| A callout | the sparkle button |
| A table | the table button, or paste one from Google Sheets or Excel |

Math still works anywhere: $\frac{3}{4}$.

modules.title: Worksheets
modules.body:
Students only ever read a Content card. When they should write, make a Question card and pick **Worksheet** under How students answer. Your text is the worksheet: headings, prompts, a table with empty cells.

**Who fills it in** has three choices:

- **Each student**: each fills in their own copy (tables too) and presses **Hand in**.
- **Each group** and **Whole class**: one shared copy, filled in together. More on the card after next.

Their copy then waits for your feedback in Students. Select any words in it and press **Comment**: the student sees your comment on those words and can reply.

> The next card is one. Try it.

modules.title: Try it: plan a lesson in your own copy
modules.body:
## My first lesson

**Topic:** 

**What students should be able to do by the end:** 

| Card | What students do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | |
| 2 | |
| 3 | |

**The question that branches, and what each answer deals:**

modules.title: Media on a card
modules.body:
Under a card's text: Link, Upload, Draw, and Record (Audio, Video, Screen or Photo, right in the browser).

- A video can play just a part: set Watch from and to.
- Make cover puts a picture on the card's face.
- Students hand in work with the same buttons on an Open answer card.

modules.title: Record a hello
modules.body: Record a short hello for your future class: who you are, and what the first lesson is about. Use Record (your voice or a video). You can also write it instead.

modules.title: Draw your lesson
modules.body: Sketch your first lesson as a row of cards, with one branch. Use Draw, or upload a photo of a paper sketch.

modules.title: Writing together
modules.body:
With a worksheet for **Each group**, every group shares one copy. Make the groups right on the card: **Make groups**, name them, split the class at random or tap students into each group. Other cards can use the same groups from the list, and you make new ones whenever the groups change. With **Whole class**, everyone shares one.

- They write in it at the same time, live: each person's cursor shows with their name, and who's there shows above the text.
- **History** keeps a version every few minutes, with who wrote in it. Look at any version, or go back to it.
- In a group, anyone can **Hand in** for the whole group. In Students you can watch a group's copy as it's written, and write in it too.

## Tables that add up

In a table, **Σ Total** adds a row that adds up each column. Write =AVERAGE, =COUNT, =MIN or =MAX in a cell instead of =SUM for those. **Bar**, **Line** and **Pie** put a chart of the table under it. Both update as students fill the table in.

modules.title: Let students pick their group
modules.body:
Sometimes students should choose: which project, which topic, which lab slot. Make a poll (Choices, Has a right answer: No) and tick **Make groups from the answers**.

- Each option is a group. A student joins one by picking it, and can switch until you tick **Lock the groups**.
- **At most** caps each group; a full group can't be picked.
- **Students see who's in each group**, or untick it to show only how many.
- The groups are kept under the card's name. Pick them in any worksheet or discussion for Each group, and press **Move students** on the poll to change them yourself.

> The next card is one. Pick a group: the worksheet after it is filled in with that group.

modules.title: Pick your study group
modules.body: Choose the group you want to be in for the rest of the course. You can switch until the groups are locked. The next worksheet is shared with your group.

questions.text: Which group do you want to join?

modules.title: Our group's first lesson
modules.body:
## Our group's first lesson

Fill this in together: everyone in your group writes in the same copy, live.

**Topic:** 

| Card | Kind | What students do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Content | |
| 2 | Question | |
| 3 | | |

**Who on the team builds which card:**

modules.title: Just exploring? Start here
modules.body:
You picked **Just exploring**, so this card is yours: only that group gets it.

Take one lesson you already teach and turn just its first ten minutes into three cards: something to read or watch, one question, and one card that an answer deals. That's enough to see how your class takes it.

modules.title: Our class in numbers
modules.body:
## How long did this course take?

Click in the Example row and press **+ Row**, then write your name and about how many minutes you've spent on Questhand 101 so far. Everyone in the class writes in this one table; the total, the average and the chart keep up.

| Name | Minutes |
| --- | --- |
| Example | 30 |
| Total | =SUM |
| Average | =AVERAGE |

[chart: bar]

modules.title: Setting up a discussion
modules.body:
A Discussion card is a conversation, like a forum: a feed of posts, each with its replies, and replies to replies.

- Posts and replies are written like a card: formatting, lists, tables and math, and Record, Upload, Draw or Link.
- Students can select words in the card's text and **Quote** them in a post.

In its panel:

- **Who discusses**: The whole class, or Each group (each group gets its own feed; pick or make the groups there).
- **Reactions**: Likes, Votes or None. Sort the feed by Newest or Top.
- **Topics**: give two or more (e.g. Questions, Ideas), and students tag each post with one; everyone can filter by topic.
- **Each student replies to**: No one, or 1 to 3 classmates. The card is done once they've posted and replied.
- **Structured feedback**: a reply to a classmate's post has three parts (what I noticed, the effect it had on me, one thing to try next), and the post's author can mark it helpful. Good for peer review of work students post: the card after next is one.
- Hide names from classmates, and I approve posts before others see them.

Type **@** in a post or reply to mention a classmate or the teacher: pick a name from the list, and they're told. Students are also told when someone replies to them.

modules.title: Introduce yourself
modules.body: Post a line about you and what you teach. Then reply to one classmate: try a voice reply (Record → Audio).

modules.title: Peer review: your lesson plan
modules.body:
Post your lesson plan (a few lines, a picture of it, or the worksheet you filled in last week). Then give feedback on two plans from your group.

Each reply has three parts: **what I noticed**, **the effect it had on me**, and **one thing to try next**. When you get feedback you can use, mark it **Helpful**.

This card is done once you've posted and replied to two classmates.

modules.title: Why an elective?
modules.body:
An elective is a lesson students choose to take (or not). Make one from a lesson's ⋯ menu: Make it an elective. Students see it in its week on their board, with its cards face down, and press Choose.

In Settings → Electives, set how many electives each student takes.

modules.title: Reading pack
modules.body: Three short readings that go together. A card group can hold any kind of card, not only questions.

modules.title: Reading 1: small cards
modules.body: Short cards are easier to start and easier to finish. Students see progress after every card.

modules.title: Reading 2: one question per card
modules.body: One question per card makes the card tree simple: each answer deals the next card.

modules.title: Reading 3: feedback that moves
modules.body: Feedback is most useful with one thing done well and one thing to try next.

modules.title: Watch: invite your class
modules.body: Inviting by email, the class code, and letting people in.

modules.title: Three ways in
modules.body:
Every student signs in with their own Questhand account (Google, or email and password), so each one needs an email address. Then:

1. An invitation. Students → Invite students → Add students by email. Tick Email each one a personal invitation, and each gets their own link.
2. The class code (or the class link, or the QR code). Students sign in, then enter the code under As Student → Join a class.
3. Their own link, sent your way. Beside anyone on your list who hasn't joined yet, Invitation link copies a link only for them, to send in a message or a chat.

modules.title: Who can join
modules.body:
In the invite box, General access decides what the class code and link do:

- Restricted: only students you invited.
- Anyone with the link or code, after you let them in: they wait until you press Let in (or Let all in).
- Anyone with the link or code: they're in at once.

Settings → Class code and guest link: make a New code, add a Join passcode, or turn joining off.

modules.title: Your class list
modules.body:
In Students → Class list, groups and demo students, each student has Message, Invitation link (copy their own link again), Reset sign-in (if a link went to the wrong person) and Remove.

Students → Class list, groups and demo students lists the groups you've made on cards, to change or remove.

Two students in one class can't share a name, since classmates find each other by name (to @mention someone, in groups and in messages). If someone joins with a name a classmate already has, they're asked to add something, like a last initial.

Teaching with someone? Settings → Teachers → Share with teachers: they Can edit or Can view.

modules.title: Demo students
modules.body:
Demo students are made-up students on your class list, for you to try the course as. **Students → Class list, groups and demo students**: type a name (or leave it, for Demo Student A, B, C…) and press **Add a demo student**. Add as many as you need. This course has eight.

Open **Student View** and pick one: you act as them, and what you do is kept, like a real student's. It shows in Students, in groups and discussions, ready for your feedback. **Start over** clears their work. They never get email, and once real students join, class numbers leave them out.

Student View can also show **New student** (a blank test where nothing is saved) or any student in your class (a test on their board; nothing is saved).

modules.title: Messages
modules.body:
Every conversation is in your **Inbox**: click your photo at the top right. A red number on the photo says how many messages are new.

- Press **New message** and pick a student, from any of your courses. Or use **Message** beside a student in Students.
- Students write to you the same way, from the Inbox under their photo.
- Students can also message each other. To turn that off for a class, untick **Students can message each other** in Settings. Messages between students are private to them.

> A message is private to the two people in it. For something the whole class should see, post it on a Discussion card.

questions.text: A student emails you: “I entered the class code, and it says I'm waiting.” What's going on?
options: Joining is set to “after you let them in”: press Let in
questions.explain: With that setting, people who use the code wait for you. You'll see them at the top of the Map and in Students.

modules.title: Watch: try it as a student
modules.body: Student View shows exactly what a student sees. Nothing you do there is graded, and no one is notified.

modules.title: Who needs you
modules.body:
The Students tab has your class list on the left. Pick **Whole class** to see a lesson: who needs attention (Overdue, Ready for your feedback, Low quiz scores, Haven't started, Stalled; press Remind to send a short note), every student's cards, and its discussions. Pick a **student** for their whole course: work waiting for you, week by week, scores and your feedback. Tags beside each name say who needs you.

On the Map, **Where students are** shows who is on which card, and how many took each answer.

The bell at the top (Class activity) lists what students did, as it happens.

> This course's eight demo students are part-way through, so these lists aren't empty. Have a look.

modules.title: Watch: give feedback
modules.body: Work students hand in waits for you in Students: pick a student to see everything of theirs waiting for you.

modules.title: A tip on feedback
modules.body: A short voice note: what makes feedback useful.

modules.title: Feedback with more than words
modules.body:
In the review panel, write what they did well and one thing to try next. You can also record how you'd play or say it, or attach a file, and + Rate skills.

Then **Looks good**, or **Ask to revise**: the student sees a Revise tag on their board and hands in again.

Group work: a worksheet a group filled in together gets one review, for everyone in the group. For work each student did on their own, tick **Send the same feedback to everyone in** their group to give the whole group one note.

modules.title: Class sessions
modules.body:
This lesson has a class session (look at its ⋯ menu). Add a class session to any lesson: an agenda of timed parts, and parts can go in turns.

In class, press Run the class session (or r). It fills the screen with a timer, the agenda and who speaks next. Live adds Hands, a Quick poll and a Random picker. At the end, Send notes to students.

modules.title: Share one idea
modules.body: What will your first Questhand lesson be about? Post one idea, and reply to someone else's.

agenda.label: Warm-up: what did your branch do?
Show your first lesson, in turns

modules.title: Final check
modules.body: Five questions, two tries. Your score decides your last card.

questions.text: How does a student get a card that an answer deals?
options: The teacher sends it by hand
questions.explain: The answer deals it: only students who pick it get the card.

questions.text: Can one answer deal more than one card?
options: Yes: drag its dot to each card
questions.explain: Drag the same answer's dot onto another card and a second line appears.

questions.text: Where do you try the course as a student, with nothing graded?
A student handed in work. Where is it waiting?
options: In Students, ready for your feedback
Nowhere until they finish the course
One thing done well, one thing to try next

modules.title: Let's go over it
modules.body:
No problem: these are the five things to remember.

1. Answers deal cards; only students who pick an answer get its card.
2. One answer can deal several cards.
3. Student View is a safe test: nothing is graded.
4. Handed-in work waits in Students.
5. Feedback: one thing done well, one to try next.

Then take the final check again.

modules.title: You're ready
modules.body: Full marks. Go and build your first lesson: one Content card, one question, and one branch. Your students will feel the difference.

modules.title: What will you build first?
modules.body: One or two sentences: the lesson you'll build first, and the branch you'll put in it.
